translation:
Sound and material both issuing is called vomiting (ou); there is material without sound, see it, treat as vomiting (tu). Sound without material is named dry retching; its sound is light, small, short and faint.
Hiccup-reflux (yue) has sound likewise and no material; its sound is loud and heavy, turbid, long-held. Swallowing-reversal (fange) — after eating, it comes then vomits; also there is the morning-eaten evening-vomited one.
Diaphragm-obstruction (yege): desiring to eat, hard to admit into mouth. Nausea: desire to vomit and not vomit — strange. Swallowing-sour: swallowing, sour gastric fluids; vomiting-acid: surging out like thin water.
Hi-cough (kuonin/欸逆), commonly called hiccup; the wa-sound erupting, the state is devious. Eructation (aiqi) is now the yawn; thick phlegm, damp-heat confused within the stomach.
Tatters and hems are nothing beyond phlegm caused by fire; pain or no pain, hungry or not hungry. For the most part it is a spleen-stomach and lung-liver illness; forehead sweat and mouth foam portend danger without doubt.
Urine and stool both not blocked, no hindrance — Baozhong Tang Yin (Protect-the-Centre Beverage) let it gallop. Shunqi Hezhong (Smooth-Qi Harmonize-the-Centre) with addition and subtraction; feel the pulse, according to the season, then adapt the treatment.

Baozhong Tang (Protect-the-Centre Decoction): treats eating and drinking not going down, vomiting and diarrhea not stopping.
Within Baozhong Tang are Huoxiang (Pogostemon) and Fuling (Poria); Huanglian (Coptis), Zhizi (Gardenia) and Ban-Sha (Pinellia & Sharen). Fuling and Chenpi with prepared Gancao (Licorice); add Longdan (Gentian) and the effect is like a spirit.
In Shunqi Tang (Smooth-Qi Decoction) Xiangfu (Cyperus) and Qin (Scutellaria); Chenpi, Gancao (Licorice), Ban-Sha (Pinellia & Sharen). Zhu (Atractylodes), Zhi (Zhike/Bitter Orange), Lian-Zhi (Coptis & Gardenia) and Shenqu (Medicated Leaven) gathered; one piece of roasted ginger ensures peace and tranquility.
translator_notes: 嘔/吐/乾嘔=ou/tu/dry retching; 噦=yuè hiccup; 噎膈=diaphragm obstruction; 噁心=nausea; 吞酸/吐酸=swallowing/vomiting acid.
保中湯=Baozhong Tang; 順氣和中湯=Shunqi Hezhong.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
The Classics say qi is the filling of the body, circulating with the blood, matched to the beginning and end. Interior and exterior contraction make the illness erupt; public and private depression and suppression, exhausted by profit and fame.
Excess (of qi) is fire burning the wild plain; insufficiency engenders cold within a square inch (the heart). Dushen (Alone-Ginseng) since antiquity has been the good method; if it is not deficient-cold, do not heedlessly follow it.

Dushen Tang (Alone-Ginseng Decoction)
Renshen (Ginseng) one liang

Qi is what all things take to begin. Heaven, without this qi, is not sufficient to nourish the ten-thousand things; man, without this qi, is not sufficient to be born. Therefore it is said: one breath not transported, then the mechanism becomes truly exhausted; one hair not continued, then evening and dawn part company. Therefore in illness, qi is the foremost concern. Renshen tastes sweet, nature warm, obtaining the central-and-harmonious qi of heaven and earth to take shape, therefore use it to supplement the central harmonious qi. Making its one breath still remain, then one can proceed by degrees and heal the various illnesses. In vexation and agitation add urine of boy: deficiency with fire. Body cold add Fuzi: to return its solitary yang. The distinction of deficiency and repletion one cannot but examine. Dushen can only treat deficiency. If it be a replete condition, critical and urgent, one should suit the season and adapt the treatment.

To treat qi deficiency use Sijunzi Tang (Four-Gentleman Decoction)
Renshen (Ginseng), Baizhu, Fuling, Sharen, Chenpi, ginger-juice-stir-fried Houpu, Dang Gui, Gancao (Licorice) each equal parts, Shengjiang one slice, Zao (Jujube) two pieces.
Deficiency severe add Huangqi.
translator_notes: 獨參湯=Dushen Tang; 四君子湯=Sijunzi Tang.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）

translation:
Glomus-pi same as the character no (否) — not free and unimpeded; not the glomus-block (píkuài) of the five accumulations. The transport-wheel loses its constancy, or is wrongly purged (down): treating dampness in the same way, like the resolve-the-glomus secret.
Replete glomus: hard stool; deficient glomus: free stool. Inside, though full and oppressed, outside there is no harm. Muxiang Huazhi (Aucklandia Dissolve-Stagnation) first try it; Huanglian Xiaoji (Coptis Resolve-Glomus) then add on thereafter.
Muxiang Huazhi (Aucklandia Dissolve-Stagnation) with Dang Gui tip; Chai (Chaihu/Bupleurum), Zhi (Zhike/Bitter Orange), Chenpi and Dafupi (Areca Peel) wrapping. Baidoukou (White Nutmeg/Cardamom), Honghua (Safflower), Jiang (shengjiang) and Banxia (Pinellia); the thatch-choked middle province, let you cast it.

Huanglian Xiaoji Wan (Coptis Resolve-Glomus Pill)
Huanglian (Coptis, earth-stir-fried), Huangqin (Scutellaria) seven qian, Zhishi (Immature Bitter Orange) five qian, Banxia, Chenpi four qian, Fuling one liang, Zhuling three qian, Zexie (Alisma), Yujin (Curcuma), Ganjiang (Dried Ginger).

Nourish-the-Stomach Method
Xiangfu (Cyperus), Sharen, Muxiang (Aucklandia), Zhishi (Immature Bitter Orange), stir-fried each seven qian, Baizhu, Fuling, Banxia, ginger-juice-stir-fried, Chenpi each one qian, Baidoukou, Huoxiang (Pogostemon), Houpu, ginger-juice-stir-fried, prepared Gancao (Licorice) two qian, Shengjiang two slices, Zao (Jujube) one piece.
Take after meals. Thin persons with glomus-fullness below the heart, add Huanglian, remove Banxia. Blood deficiency add Dang Gui, Baishao, remove Banxia. Phlegm-hindered diaphragm add Gualou ren (Trichosanthes seed), Beimu (Fritillaria), Jiegeng (Platycodon), Zhuli (Bamboo juice), a little ginger juice, Baizhu, Banxia. Spleen-diarrhea add stir-fried Cangzhu, Baishao, remove Banxia.
translator_notes: 木香化滯湯=Muxiang Huazhi Tang; 黃連消痞丸=Huanglian Xiaoji Wan.
否=pi (obstruction) gloss relating to 痞.
book: 七十二症辨治方法（手抄本）
